📚 Today you learned

Analyst Price Target Dispersion

A single "average price target" hides how much analysts actually agree. Look at the spread instead. GOOG's targets today range from Raymond James's $400 to Pivotal's $470 around a $428 consensus — a ~16% spread, tight, because the bull case (Cloud, Search, AI capex payoff) is broadly shared even if the exact number isn't. SPXC's range is $225 to $310 around ~$272 — a ~38% spread, more than double GOOG's, because analysts genuinely disagree on how much the Kranze defense exposure and slowing HVAC momentum should discount the stock. Wide dispersion isn't noise to average away — it's the market telling you the name carries real, unresolved uncertainty. When you see a wide spread on a position you're holding, that's your cue to have your own clear thesis rather than leaning on "the average target," because the average is averaging over analysts who fundamentally disagree with each other.

Also today: GF Value / intrinsic value estimate — GuruFocus's own DCF-style fair-value model, used today to call SPXC "5.5% overvalued" at $200.90 despite the pullback; one more independent read alongside analyst targets, not a replacement for your own.
